sentences.text: This animal was a small, four-legged plant-eater reaching a total length of about 2 meters.

Its scientific name translates to 'ischium horned face,' highlighting a unique bone shape where the lower hip bone resembles a curved bow flaring into a rectangular section with an elliptical opening.
Scientists consider this specific hip bone structure a single defining trait found only in this dinosaur among all known species.
It remains one of the few known horned-face dinosaurs for which no skull fossils have been discovered.
A distinct ridge on the upper part of its tail formed a crest, a feature also seen in other members of its group.
The genus was named and described in 2015 by a team of seven researchers including He Yiming and Xu Xing.
The primary specimen used to define the species was found in Kugou, Shandong Province, China.
Phylogenetic analysis confirms Ischioceratops as a member of the Leptoceratopsidae family with Montanoceratops as its closest relative.
It is distinguished within this family by having nine sacral vertebrae.
Ischioceratops lived approximately 77.3 to 73.5 million years ago in the Wangshi Group during the late Cretaceous period.
Its environment included centrosaurines, saurolophines, and tyrannosaurines.
The recorded time range for this species spans the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
